extraction.name: airbench94
extraction.description: A training method for CIFAR-10 that achieves 94% accuracy in 3.29 seconds, 95% in 10.4 seconds, and 96% in 46.3 seconds on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU. The method introduces a derandomized variant of horizontal flipping augmentation (alternating flip) which improves training speed over standard random flipping. The code is released at https://github.com/KellerJordan/cifar10-airbench.
extraction.creator: Keller Jordan
extraction.citeAs: Keller Jordan. (2024). 94% on CIFAR-10 in 3.29 Seconds on a Single GPU. arXiv:2404.00498v2 [cs.LG]
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The CIFAR-10 dataset is used, which contains 60,000 32x32 color images divided into a training set of 50,000 images and a validation set of 10,000 images. The dataset is a standard benchmark in machine learning, widely used for image classification tasks.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: CIFAR-10 dataset (Krizhevsky et al., 2009), which is a standard benchmark dataset in machine learning.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The training method introduces a derandomized variant of horizontal flipping augmentation called 'alternating flip,' which deterministically alternates flipping of images after the first epoch to avoid redundancy and speed up training. Additionally, the method includes frozen patch-whitening initialization, identity initialization for convolutions, optimization tricks (e.g., increased learning rate for BatchNorm biases, Lookahead optimizer), and multi-crop evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The CIFAR-10 dataset is preprocessed using normalization (CIFAR_MEAN and CIFAR_STD values). The training data is augmented with random horizontal flipping and 2-pixel random translation (using reflection padding). Test-time augmentation (TTA) is applied using horizontal flipping and two extra crops for evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset is labeled as part of the CIFAR-10 dataset, with each image labeled as one of ten classes. No additional annotation protocol is described beyond the standard CIFAR-10 labeling.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The code and methods are released as the 'airbench' Python package, with versioning information available at the GitHub repository. The package includes scripts for achieving 94%, 95%, and 96% accuracy targets on CIFAR-10.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is a standard benchmark (CIFAR-10), and while biases are not explicitly discussed, the method's focus on training speed and efficiency may introduce biases in terms of computational resource usage and environmental impact.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The method is specifically designed for CIFAR-10 and may not generalize optimally to other datasets without re-tuning. The training speed improvements are measured on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU, and the method's effectiveness may vary on different hardware. The use of test-time augmentation (TTA) increases inference time, which may be a limitation in some applications.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. The method is intended to accelerate research and reduce the cost of experiments involving CIFAR-10. It is particularly useful for projects requiring rapid experimental iteration or a massive number of trained networks.
